common.whyIntro: Women and girls in Kakuma Refugee Camp face many challenges, including financial hardship, interrupted education, limited access to skills training, and barriers to employment and healthcare. For teenage mothers, these challenges can be even greater as they balance childcare with their education and personal development. At Women Without Borders Hub, we believe every girl and young woman deserves the opportunity to overcome these barriers, discover her potential, and build a better future. By promoting education, practical skills, mentorship, health awareness, and economic empowerment, we aim to create opportunities for women and girls to grow in confidence, strengthen their independence, and contribute to their communities.

secondChanceDetail.intro: We support girls and women in Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kenya, who wish to continue their education, overcome barriers to learning, and build a better future. We believe that education is a right and that every girl and woman deserves the opportunity to learn, grow, and reach her full potential.
secondChanceDetail.whatImageAlt: A woman studying during a learning session
whatParagraphs: Our Second Chance Education programme focuses on supporting girls and women whose education has been interrupted or who have not had the opportunity to complete their studies. We recognize that financial difficulties, family responsibilities, displacement, and other life challenges can make it difficult to continue learning. Through this programme, we promote the importance of returning to education and encourage girls and women to pursue their learning goals with confidence and determination.

We believe that access to education can help women and girls gain knowledge, strengthen their independence, participate more actively in their communities, and create better opportunities for themselves and their families.

srhrDetail.title: Promoting Knowledge, Dignity, and Informed Choices
intro: At Women Without Borders Hub, we believe that every girl and young woman deserves access to reliable information about her sexual and reproductive health in a safe, respectful, and supportive environment.

In Kakuma Refugee Camp, stigma, cultural barriers, limited awareness, and difficulty accessing accurate health information can make it hard for some young people to discuss sexual and reproductive health openly. Our SRHR programme promotes age-appropriate education, peer learning, and community awareness to help address these challenges.

intro: Economic empowerment is an important step toward helping women and girls build secure, independent, and dignified lives. Through our Livelihood & Economic Empowerment programme, Women Without Borders Hub aims to support women and young people in developing practical skills, exploring income-generating opportunities, strengthening their confidence, and working toward greater financial independence.

We recognize that many women and girls face barriers that limit their ability to access education, employment, business opportunities, and the resources needed to support themselves and their families. These challenges can include limited access to vocational training, financial resources, business knowledge, professional networks, and employment opportunities.

As a community-based organization located in Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kenya, we seek to help address these barriers by promoting practical learning, entrepreneurship, mentorship, and connections to available opportunities. We believe that every woman and girl deserves the chance to discover her potential, develop useful skills, and participate meaningfully in her community.

Our goal is to encourage sustainable livelihoods that help women and girls strengthen their independence, improve their economic prospects, and contribute positively to their households and communities.

sections.title: Why Livelihood & Economic Empowerment Matters
paragraphs: When women and girls have access to relevant skills, knowledge, mentorship, and economic opportunities, they are better positioned to explore ways of improving their circumstances and planning for the future.

Livelihood opportunities can help individuals work toward greater financial independence, strengthen their ability to meet everyday needs, and contribute to the well-being of their households. They can also encourage creativity, resilience, problem-solving, and community participation.

For women and girls living in challenging circumstances, including displacement and limited access to resources, opportunities for skills development and economic participation can be especially important. However, sustainable progress requires more than individual effort. It also depends on supportive communities, accessible training, relevant opportunities, and partnerships that respond to real needs.
At Women Without Borders Hub, we believe that investing in women's skills, ideas, and potential is an important part of building stronger and more inclusive communities.

sections.title: Who We Aim to Support
paragraphs: Our Livelihood & Economic Empowerment programme is intended to support women and girls who want to develop their skills, explore economic opportunities, and work toward greater independence.

Our focus includes women and young women in the community, girls preparing for future livelihood opportunities, and individuals who face barriers to skills development, entrepreneurship, or employment. We recognize that each participant has different experiences, responsibilities, interests, and goals.
We therefore value approaches that respect individual circumstances and help participants identify realistic pathways suited to their abilities and aspirations.

sections.title: Working Together to Create Opportunities
paragraphs: Sustainable economic empowerment requires collaboration. Community organizations, local businesses, employers, training institutions, mentors, donors, and development partners can all play a role in expanding access to knowledge, skills, resources, and opportunities.
Women Without Borders Hub welcomes engagement with partners who share our commitment to supporting women and girls through livelihood development and economic participation.

Potential areas of collaboration include vocational and entrepreneurship training, mentorship, business development support, apprenticeship opportunities, market connections, employment referrals, and resources for community-based livelihood initiatives.
By working together, we can help create more opportunities for women and girls to develop their potential, pursue their goals, and contribute to a more inclusive and resilient community.

whatWeDo.title: What We Do
intro: Livelihood & Economic Empowerment is one of our core programme areas. We work alongside women and girls, community members, educators, local organizations, and potential partners to identify barriers and explore practical ways to expand access to economic opportunities.

Our programme focuses on building knowledge, confidence, practical abilities, and connections that can help participants take steps toward employment, entrepreneurship, and sustainable income generation.

areas.title: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: We promote entrepreneurship as one possible pathway toward economic independence. Through business learning and mentorship opportunities, women and girls can explore how to identify business ideas, understand customer needs, plan their activities, and develop the knowledge needed to manage a small business.

Topics may include identifying business opportunities, basic business planning, budgeting, record-keeping, customer service, pricing, marketing, and managing income and expenses. These skills can help aspiring entrepreneurs make informed decisions and approach business activities with greater confidence.

We also recognize the importance of learning from people with practical business experience. Where opportunities are available, connecting participants with local entrepreneurs and business mentors can help them understand common challenges and learn from real-life experiences.

areas.title: Skills Development and Vocational Training
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Skills Development and Vocational Training activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Practical skills can open doors to employment, self-employment, and other livelihood opportunities. We aim to encourage access to relevant skills development and vocational learning that responds to the interests of participants and the needs of the local community.

Depending on available training opportunities and partnerships, this may include practical, technical, creative, or service-related skills that can help participants prepare for work or explore small income-generating activities.

Our approach emphasizes the value of continuous learning, practical experience, and the confidence to apply newly acquired skills. We seek to support pathways through which women and girls can identify their strengths and make informed decisions about their future.

areas.title: Business Mentorship and Guidance
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Business Mentorship and Guidance activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Starting a business or pursuing employment can be challenging, especially for people who have limited access to professional networks and experienced advisers. Mentorship can help participants explore their goals, understand potential challenges, and identify realistic next steps.

Through mentorship opportunities, women and girls may receive guidance on setting goals, developing business ideas, improving decision-making, building confidence, and identifying resources that could support their progress.

We value mentorship that respects each participant's circumstances and encourages them to recognize their abilities. By learning from others and sharing experiences, participants can develop a stronger understanding of the opportunities available to them.

areas.title: Apprenticeships and Work Experience
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Apprenticeships and Work Experience activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Practical work experience can help bridge the gap between learning and employment. Where suitable opportunities are available, we seek to encourage connections with skilled professionals, businesses, training providers, and other community partners that may offer apprenticeships or supervised learning experiences.

These opportunities can help participants gain practical knowledge, understand workplace expectations, develop professional habits, and become more familiar with the skills required in different fields.
Work-based learning can also help participants identify their interests, strengthen their confidence, and explore possible pathways toward employment or self-employment.

areas.title: Market Linkages and Networking
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Market Linkages and Networking activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Access to customers, suppliers, professional contacts, and reliable information can make a difference for people who want to develop their livelihoods. We recognize that having a skill or business idea is only one part of the journey; participants may also need connections that help them find customers and explore markets.

Through potential partnerships and community networks, we aim to encourage opportunities for women and girls to learn about market needs, connect with relevant service providers, share ideas, and identify possible routes for promoting their products or services.
Stronger networks can help participants exchange knowledge, learn from other entrepreneurs, and explore opportunities to grow their activities over time.

areas.title: Employment Readiness and Referrals
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Employment Readiness and Referrals activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: For women and girls who want to pursue employment, preparing for work can involve more than technical skills. Communication, teamwork, problem-solving, time management, and confidence can all be important when seeking and maintaining employment.

We aim to promote awareness of employment preparation and, where appropriate opportunities exist, connect participants with relevant training providers, employers, job information, or employment referral services.

This support may include guidance on preparing for job opportunities, understanding workplace expectations, identifying relevant skills, and exploring available career pathways. Referrals depend on the availability and suitability of opportunities and do not guarantee employment.

areas.title: Financial Awareness and Responsible Money Management
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Financial Awareness and Responsible Money Management activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Understanding how to manage money can help individuals make informed decisions about their personal finances and livelihood activities. We encourage the development of basic financial awareness, including planning expenses, saving where possible, managing business income, keeping financial records, and understanding the difference between costs, revenue, and profit.
These skills can support participants as they plan for their needs, evaluate business ideas, and work toward their financial goals.

We also recognize that financial circumstances differ from person to person. Our approach aims to promote practical, realistic learning that respects participants' situations and supports informed decision-making.

areas.title: Confidence, Leadership, and Economic Participation
areas.imageAlt: Women taking part in the Confidence, Leadership, and Economic Participation activity in Kakuma
paragraphs: Economic empowerment involves more than earning an income. It also includes having the confidence to make decisions, express ideas, participate in community life, and pursue personal goals.
We encourage women and girls to recognize their strengths, develop their leadership abilities, and take an active role in decisions that affect their livelihoods and futures.
By promoting confidence, collaboration, and access to information, we aim to support participants in becoming more active contributors to their households and communities.

ourApproach.title: Our Approach
ourApproach.intro: We aim to develop livelihood initiatives that are practical, inclusive, community-informed, and responsive to the experiences of the people we serve.

items.title: Community-led design
items.text: We value the experiences, priorities, and ideas of women and girls. Listening to community members helps identify relevant needs and shape activities that are better suited to their circumstances.

items.title: Safe and inclusive participation
items.text: We aim to promote respectful learning environments where participants are treated with dignity, have opportunities to contribute, and can participate without discrimination. Safeguarding and appropriate support should remain central to programme activities.

items.title: Practical and relevant learning
items.text: We recognize the importance of skills that participants can apply in everyday life, business activities, training, or employment pathways. Activities should respond to participants' interests and available opportunities.

items.title: Mentorship and collaboration
items.text: We value cooperation with community groups, local businesses, training providers, employers, educators, and other organizations that can contribute knowledge, resources, or relevant opportunities.

items.title: Access to opportunities
items.text: Where possible, we aim to connect participants with information about training, business development, markets, apprenticeships, and employment pathways.

items.title: Learning and accountability
items.text: We seek to learn from programme activities, listen to participant feedback, and communicate progress transparently. Where activities are implemented, monitoring can help us understand participation, identify challenges, and improve future support.

building-pathways-for-women-and-girls.summary: What happens when women in Kakuma gain access to education, skills, and opportunity?
building-pathways-for-women-and-girls.fullText:
What happens when women in Kakuma gain access to education, skills, and opportunity?

Women Without Borders Hub is building pathways for women and girls in Kakuma to learn, earn, and lead.

Because when women gain access, communities gain resilience.

Women Without Borders Hub, Kakuma, is a community-led initiative empowering women and girls in Kakuma refugee camp through:

- Education,
- Health advocacy,
- Entrepreneurship,
- Technical skills development.

We are building pathways for women and girls to access the tools, knowledge, and opportunities needed to create independent futures and stronger communities.

Our work is focused on four core pillars:

- Education Advocacy
- Health Advocacy
- Entrepreneurship Advocacy
- Technical Skills Development

This is more than a program.

It is a platform for dignity, resilience, and economic inclusion.

We believe women in refugee communities should not be defined by displacement but by their circumstances, potential, leadership, and power to shape the future.

Women Without Borders Hub exists to turn access into opportunity, and opportunity into long-term transformation.

If you care about women's empowerment, refugee livelihoods, and inclusive development, we'd love to connect.

graduation-celebration-skills.fullText:
For the women of Women Without Borders Hub, this graduation was more than certificates; it was a celebration of resilience, courage, growth, and new possibilities.

Behind every certificate is a woman who chose to learn, build new skills, find her voice, and create a better future for herself, her family, and her community.

We are grateful to Teach for Community for hosting this special ceremony and celebrating these women with us.

When women learn, communities grow. When women lead, communities move forward.

Congratulations to our graduates!

health-advocacy.title: Advocating for Health: Women Without Borders Hub
health-advocacy.alt: Health advocacy for refugee and host communities in Kakuma
health-advocacy.summary: Health is a human right, not a privilege.
health-advocacy.fullText:
Health is a human right, not a privilege.

Yet many women, children, and displaced families still struggle to access basic healthcare, information, and support.

Today at Women Without Borders Hub, we are learning, engaging, and advocating for stronger health awareness and community well-being.

Through health advocacy, we believe communities become stronger, safer, and more empowered to make informed decisions about their lives and futures.

From maternal health and mental wellness to hygiene awareness and access to healthcare services, every conversation matters.

Healthy communities build stronger futures.

Awareness saves lives.

Advocacy creates change.

Together, we continue raising voices for equitable and inclusive healthcare for refugee and host communities in Kakuma and beyond.

ourStory.pageTitle: MaLua Lugazo: Building Hope for Girls in Kakuma
ourStory.lead: MaLua Lugazo is a Somali refugee living in Kakuma Refugee Camp who founded Women Without Borders Hub so that every girl and young woman has a chance to learn, grow and lead.
ourStory.photoAlt: MaLua Lugazo, Founder of Women Without Borders Hub
ourStory.quote: Every girl has the right to learn, grow and lead.
ourStory.fromKakumaText: MaLua Lugazo knows Kakuma from the inside. As a Somali refugee growing up in the camp, she watched bright girls disappear from classrooms — early marriage, pregnancy, household labour and school costs closing doors one by one. She also saw what a single opportunity could do: a scholarship, a mentor, a safe room to study in. That contrast — between what girls in Kakuma are denied and what they become when someone believes in them — is where Women Without Borders Hub began.
ourStory.whyHubText: MaLua founded Women Without Borders Hub so that no girl in Kakuma would have to fight for an education alone. The Hub brings refugee and host-community girls together in one movement: education and literacy, digital and vocational skills, mentorship, menstrual dignity, health and pathways into work. Every programme is community-led — designed with the girls it serves — because the girls of Kakuma are not a problem to be solved but leaders to be equipped.
ourStory.closingText: Today the Hub walks with vulnerable girls, teenage mothers and young women across Kakuma — from the classroom to the marketplace. Explore our programmes, see the change your support creates, and join the story:

getInvolvedCards.heading: Ways to support women and girls
getInvolvedCards.intro: There are many ways you can support our mission, from volunteering your time and sharing your skills to providing financial support, mentoring young women, or partnering with us. Every contribution matters and can help expand access to education, skills development, health awareness, and economic opportunities for women and girls in Kakuma Refugee Camp. Together, we can break barriers, build confidence, and create a future where every girl and young woman has the opportunity to thrive.

profile.title: MaLua Lugazo - Founder & Executive Director of Women Without Borders Hub
profile.heroIntro: MaLua Lugazo is the Founder and Executive Director of Women Without Borders Hub, a community-led initiative based in Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kenya. The Hub works to create opportunities for refugee and marginalized women and girls to learn, build skills and shape their own futures.
profile.photoAlt: MaLua Lugazo, Founder and Executive Director of Women Without Borders Hub
featureParagraphs: MaLua brings more than nine years of experience in humanitarian and community development. She served for five years as a Project Coordinator with Wings to Fly Initiative — CBO, and for four years as a Facilitator with the Norwegian Refugee Council, where she implemented the Accelerated Education Programme and served as a Better Learning Programme Champion.

She holds a Diploma in Social Work and Community Development and is pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Social Work and Administration. Her work has strengthened her commitment to education, community development, child protection, and creating opportunities for vulnerable and marginalized populations, particularly refugee women and girls.
motivationParagraphs: MaLua started Women Without Borders Hub after years of working alongside refugee and marginalized women and girls in Kakuma. She repeatedly saw the same pattern: women and girls were willing and ready to learn, to lead and to build a life for themselves, but they were held back by barriers that were never addressed by short-term responses.

Rather than run another short-term activity, she founded the Hub to build a space where women and girls are treated as partners and leaders in their own development. That decision is at the heart of everything the organization does today.
profile.barriersTitle: The barriers women and girls face in Kakuma
profile.barriersIntro: Living in Kakuma Refugee Camp means that opportunities are limited and competition for the few that exist is intense. The main barriers observed by the Hub are:
problemParagraphs: Women and girls in Kakuma are often excluded from the decisions that affect their lives. Programmes are designed for them rather than with them, and support stops once a project ends. As a result, the same barriers return year after year and leadership potential stays untapped.

Women Without Borders Hub responds to this gap with a community-led approach that strengthens practical skills, restores access to learning, and positions women and girls as leaders of their own solutions.
profile.focusAreasTitle: The five focus areas of the Hub
profile.missionTitle: The mission of Women Without Borders Hub
profile.mission: To empower refugee and marginalized women and girls in Kakuma by strengthening education, skills, confidence and leadership, so that they can shape their own futures and lead change in their community.
profile.challengesIntro: As Founder and Executive Director, MaLua leads the organization day to day while also shaping its long-term direction. The main challenges she leads on are:
profile.changeTitle: The change she wants to see
changeParagraphs: MaLua wants to see women and girls in Kakuma move from being seen only as beneficiaries to being recognized as partners and leaders. She wants the barriers that stop girls from returning to school, from learning new skills and from earning their own income to weaken, and she wants more women included in the decisions that shape their community.
For the Hub, this means young women leaving school with new skills and confidence, women earning a steady income, and girls stepping into leadership roles in their families, schools and community.
profile.longTermVision: MaLua envisions Women Without Borders Hub growing into a strong, self-sustaining community organization that is led by the women and girls it serves. The long-term goal is for the Hub to become a model of community-led change in Kakuma and beyond, proving that local leadership is the most powerful force for lasting change, and inspiring other organizations to work differently.
profile.closing: Every contribution helps more women and girls in Kakuma access education, skills and the space to lead.
